evidence_policy: Model choices below are justified from the problem structure and engineering/statistical requirements, not from public-solution scores.

mathematical_translation.sample: one 1024-point magnetic-flux-density waveform plus operating-condition metadata
key_invariance: classification should depend mainly on shape, not absolute amplitude
representation should be robust to moderate scale and phase/start-index differences

baseline.model: template/rule classifier on normalized shape descriptors
baseline.why: Three classes have strong geometric signatures; a transparent baseline reveals whether complex ML is even necessary.

primary.model: SVM or RandomForest on immutable engineered waveform features
primary.recommended_default: RandomForest if nonlinear feature interactions dominate; SVM if features are compact and standardized
feature_groups: time-domain: range, RMS, crest factor, skewness, kurtosis
shape: slope quantiles, slope sign changes, flat-top ratio, derivative dispersion
why: easy to validate and explain under contest time

use_when: engineered features fail on ambiguous or phase-shifted waveforms
sample size is sufficient and grouped validation shows a real gain
reject_as_default_because: higher chance of learning incidental sampling details

validation: group/diagnostic splits by material, temperature or frequency bands
stress test after amplitude normalization and small circular phase shifts
Q1.decision_rule: Use the simplest feature representation that preserves grouped-validation performance. A random holdout score alone does not justify a stronger generalization claim.

Q2.problem_structure: named physics-model calibration and interpretable temperature extension

primary.equation: log P = c0 + alpha log f + beta log Bm + gamma1*DeltaT + gamma2*DeltaT^2
why: quadratic term can capture monotone or curved temperature effect without making every exponent temperature-dependent
primary.complexity_guard: Drop gamma2 when not supported by leave-one-temperature-out validation.

alternatives.use_when: residuals show temperature changes mainly scale but not frequency/Bm elasticity
clear residual interaction T×log(f) or T×log(Bm) is reproducible
parametric temperature form is consistently inadequate
alternatives.role: diagnostic/benchmark, not first replacement for the requested interpretable correction

validation: leave-one-temperature-out: hold out 25/50/70/90 C in turn
Q2.Bm_definition: Prefer half peak-to-peak Bm=(max B-min B)/2 unless the problem statement or engineering convention clearly specifies otherwise; compare with max(|B|) if offset exists.
Q2.decision_rule: Choose the least complex temperature correction that improves held-out-temperature error, not the one with the lowest training SSE.

Q3.problem_structure: factor main effects + requested two-way interactions under important continuous covariates
Q3.response: log(core loss) unless diagnostics show raw-scale residuals are acceptable

primary.model: ANCOVA / robust linear model with categorical main effects and all requested two-way interactions
primary.formula: log P ~ log f + log Bm + T + W + M + T:W + T:M + W:M
why: supports interpretable adjusted means and effect sizes
inference: effect size such as partial eta-squared / standardized contrasts

baseline.model: adjusted group means after simple covariate regression
baseline.why: easy sanity check; not enough alone for interaction conclusions

alternative.model: GAM or tree ensemble + grouped permutation importance
alternative.not_for: replacing the explicit inferential interaction model

Q3.interpretation_guard: Call results conditional associations/effects within the fitted model, not causal effects unless a causal design is justified.

Q4.problem_structure: heterogeneous engineering regression with waveform + operating conditions
Q4.target: log(core loss) as default candidate because loss spans orders of magnitude; verify by residual diagnostics

primary.model: gradient-boosted trees on engineered features, with a physics baseline retained
primary.upgrade: physics + residual model if cross-condition validation is more stable than pure black-box prediction

validation.regime_A: stratified random CV by temperature x material x waveform
validation.regime_B: leave-one-condition diagnostics such as leave-one-temperature-out and, if supported by data, leave-one-material-out
validation.distribution_check: compare train/test ranges and nearest-neighbor/support distance

Q4.decision_rule: Do not call a model 'best' from random CV alone. Prefer the model that preserves accuracy under the deployment-relevant grouped regime.

Q5.problem_structure: mixed discrete-continuous bi-objective optimization over a learned surrogate

discrete: temperature if restricted to experimental levels

baseline.model: enumerate discrete groups + Latin-hypercube/dense sampling in (f,Bm) + nondominated filtering

primary.model: NSGA-II / nondominated evolutionary search with explicit two-objective vector
primary.why: directly preserves the multiobjective structure and mixed-variable search

alternative.form: min P_hat subject to f*Bm >= E0, sweep E0
alternative.strength: high interpretability and no arbitrary fixed weights

avoid_as_default.reason: requires preference/normalization assumptions and may miss non-convex Pareto regions

support_constraints: per material/waveform experimental frequency and Bm ranges
no extrapolation to unobserved categorical combinations
report whether an optimum sits on a boundary
output: representative knee/ideal-distance solution only after declaring the preference rule
sensitivity of recommended condition to model uncertainty
Q5.decision_rule: Optimizer choice comes after objective completeness and feasible-domain definition.

cross_question_consistency: Q1 waveform representation should feed Q4/Q5 consistently when test waveform labels are unknown.
Q2 physical baseline should be retained as a comparator in Q4.
Q3 factor findings can guide interpretation but must not leak test labels or replace Q4 validation.
Q4 predictor used in Q5 must carry an applicability/support-domain contract.
